added_failure_basis: the reviewed run records no baseline_suite/after_suite pair (its declared write paths held no test file, so its suite fence was unarmed); at head 9686881f1 the focused gate logs/joint-acceptance-gate.log reads 9 passed EXIT=0 and the adjacent contracts logs/adjacent-acceptance-contracts.log read 22 passed EXIT=0, and the only red in the run is the declared mutation arm logs/joint-acceptance-mutation.log (1 failed by id, EXIT=1), which is the negative control and not an added failure

findings.text: _residual_only() treats every value except the empty string and "0" as enabling, so NOVA_JOINT_ACCEPTANCE_RESIDUAL_ONLY=false (or "no", "off") silently reduces the production predicate to the global residual and admits the strong-1000 class of state; parse an explicit truthy set instead.

when null_position is required but no clause key ends in ".axis", the branch appends one not_measured verdict and continues, dropping every declared X-point clause from the receipt, against the module's "a verdict per clause" contract; the row is still incomplete, so the overall state stays safe.

ATTRIBUTES is exported in __all__ and placed in _FAMILY_ORDER, but it appears in no kind's _REQUIRED or _EXCLUDED, so any attributes clause is always judged not_applicable and the exported name promises a judging path that does not exist.
_passing_lane_clauses is defined and never called, so its lane bounds are dead code and a reader cannot tell whether the passing-lane control was dropped from the suite.

the worked centroid clause set collapses every constraint row into one sup judged against min(row_tolerance_pitches), so a row inside its own declared tolerance but above the tightest row's is refused, and the done_when's "each constraint row at its declared scale" is exercised nowhere even though evaluate() supports it.

justifications.durability: tests/test_joint_acceptance.py:266 reddens when the predicate reverts to the residual alone (logs/joint-acceptance-mutation.log FAILED by id), but no test declares an X-point clause, so the half of the one-pitch bound covering admitted X-points (nova/equilibrium/joint_acceptance.py:397) is unguarded.
justifications.evidence: the refusal is read from an independent receipt whose own values were re-read (net_boundary_level_over_span -0.0274 against boundary_limit_over_span 0.001 at docs/figures/centroid-constrained-oracle-solve/certificate-ladder-500-1000-probe/strong-rotation-compact-static-1000.json), and the mutation log is a real red by id; the run files no baseline/after suite pair, so the count rests on the focused gate and adjacent contracts, both green.
justifications.fit: the module follows the frozen-dataclass and module-constant idiom of nova/equilibrium/observable_acceptance.py:1, ruff check passes, and both commit messages carry bodies with no AI trailer and no plan identifier, but nova/equilibrium/joint_acceptance.py:74 exports ATTRIBUTES, a family no kind ever judges.
justifications.goal_fidelity: nova/equilibrium/joint_acceptance.py:326 evaluates every applicable family and returns a ClauseVerdict per clause, but support_stability and boundary_class are judged by kind (only AIR_CORE) rather than by declaration as the done_when words it, so a non-air-core row declaring them is recorded not_applicable (nova/equilibrium/joint_acceptance.py:146).
justifications.reuse: a search over nova/equilibrium found only nova/equilibrium/observable_acceptance.py:203, which judges registered observables of a throughput batch and owns a different capability; plan section 7 records no predicate existing, so the addition neither extends nor forks an owner.
